open_items: Confirm whether the S1 follow-up univariate F statistics printed as intervention effects are actually intervention rather than discipline effects. The reconciled form flags the labels; the source provides no corrected table or analysis output (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1439; PDF p. 10, printed p. 1440). They remain as printed pending reconciliation, without recalculation.

Exact distinct-person randomized and analyzed counts, per-arm counts, attendance, consent, duplicate removal, and exclusions by study are not reported. Degrees of freedom and rounded table entries must not be converted into person counts (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1437; PDF p. 8, printed p. 1438; PDF p. 9, printed p. 1439).
Identify the unlabeled parenthetical values in Tables 1-2 and obtain participant-level dispersion and uncertainty if available. No SD or SE is inferred from these values (PDF p. 10, printed p. 1440).

Full-sample S1 arm means and signed differences are not printed; only per-discipline means and the disputed full-sample test labels are available (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1439; PDF p. 10, printed p. 1440).

Clarify numeric rubric coding, how raters were aggregated, and the effective analysis unit. Participant unit and se_basis reflect the per-respondent submission analysis, but the paper does not state the aggregation rule or a blinding protocol (PDF p. 8, printed p. 1438). Discussion says evaluators could identify AI-assisted submissions from their quantity of responses (PDF p. 11, printed p. 1441).

Management originality prints denominator df = 198 while fluency and elaboration print 120. It also prints p = .06 in text versus .064 in Table 2. The printed df are retained and the more precise table p-value is used; original output is needed to settle the df discrepancy (PDF p. 10, printed p. 1440).

The Management analysis is described as having Discipline (Entrepreneurship vs Marketing) as its sole independent variable, despite being reported as a Management intervention comparison. Its omnibus Wilks Lambda is also flagged as inconsistent in the reconciled screening. No corrections can be established from the saved source (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1439; PDF p. 10, printed p. 1440).
Randomization mechanics are not stated beyond individual assignment within discipline before class (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1437).

The extent of participant overlap between the subject cohorts after duplicate removal is not reported. No shared sample with another paper is identified in the reconciled form (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1437).

The study country and AI release year are not explicitly stated; country remains not_stated and ai_tool.year remains null. Author affiliations do not establish the study location (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1432; PDF p. 7, printed p. 1437).
notes: Extractor A; completed 2026-10-10. Read the complete markdown conversion, including the final references; no appendix or supplement is included or identified. Checked cited source pages with pymupdf and recovered the result tables using text-based table detection. Retained the reconciled two-study structure: the paperclip-task analysis combines Entrepreneurship and Marketing; Management has a separate workplace-ideation task and analysis. S1 discipline-specific cells remain named in the study arm map, but their contrasts are excluded from estimates as subgroup results under extraction-spec rules 4-5, notwithstanding the screening suggestion to use those contrasts while the pooled labels remain unresolved. All assignment and analysis counts remain null: recruitment enrollments include students in multiple subjects and precede duplicate removal and other exclusions. Counts of classes are not randomized clusters because assignment was to individual students. AI-versus-usual-resources contrasts are ai_vs_bau; internet searching was permitted as part of ordinary resources rather than assigned as an active comparator. The phrase calling fluency the primary index of creative ideation occurs in the rationale for dropping flexibility, not a preregistered primary-outcome declaration. No preregistration, data/code availability statement, across-people diversity outcome, or post-AI unassisted outcome is reported. All estimates concern outputs made during the assigned task. No means were pooled, differences calculated, sample sizes inferred, or dispersion statistics converted; source quotations preserve printed precision. The study used ChatGPT-3.5; the acknowledgement of ChatGPT-4 concerns manuscript editing, not the experimental intervention (PDF p. 13, printed p. 1443). The supplied mechanical checker has a comma-normalization limitation for degrees of freedom printed without a space, such as F(1,198); these df and the unchanged verbatim quotations were independently matched to the exact cited PDF pages.
